title: Opus host, gpt-5.6-luna delegates (Claude Opus code critic), 3 h fences

roster.ruling: Benchmark missions run their host on Opus, never Fable (human, 2026-08-05). Delegates run gpt-5.6-luna, not gpt-5.6-sol: the human capped cost explicitly on the same day, before any benchmark had ever run, and an unmeasured per-run cost is not a thing to discover with the expensive model. | 2026-08-18: Wido ruled the code critic runs on claude/claude-opus-5 as bm-1's STANDING roster — a fresh ruling this date (his mission-scoped vm-smoke-5 option-A answer inspired it but authorized one mission only, per the issue-8/7 critique); implementer and design critic stay on gpt-5.6-luna under the 2026-08-05 cost ruling.

fences.approved: 2026-08-05, under the human's blanket approval; still an experiment per the promotion rule

exposure.note: EUR:40 is the TOTAL run ceiling Wido re-confirmed on 2026-08-18 for the MIXED roster: Opus host, gpt-5.6-luna design/implementation delegates, and the claude-opus-5 code critic all spend under this one figure; the sealed host.max-budget-usd=5.00 bounds host spend per turn only, not the total. Revised down from EUR:75 when the human first capped cost; the first trial's recorded usage recalibrates it.

notes.roster: Pinned by exact model identifier when a run is prepared, never by a phrase like 'cheap models', because comparability requires two cohorts to share an identical roster.
notes.fences: Provisional and unapproved. These are an experiment, not a belief: trial runs record what they consume and each fence becomes ceil(observed_max * 1.5), excluding trials that parked at that fence. A human must approve them before any run spends money.
